People / community

Yaquina

The Yaquina are an Indigenous people of Oregon’s central coast. Their traditional homeland includes the Yaquina River valley and Yaquina Bay. The Yaquina are one of the ancestral peoples of the Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians.

Selected reading

01

Homeland and name

Oregon’s Tribal History/Shared History curriculum explains that Yaqona names the river valley in the Alsea and Yaquina languages. English usage extended Yaquina to the people and to places such as the river, bay, and headland.

Read the sources [1] Oregon Department of Education; Tribal History/Shared History

02

Villages and connections to Siletz

Historian and archaeologist R. Scott Byram describes Yaquina villages around the bay and smaller settlements on rivers and tributaries before the mid-1850s. He identifies the Yaquina as one of the ancestral peoples of today’s Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians.

Read the sources [2] Oregon Historical Quarterly

Colonial Power and Indigenous Justice: Fur Trade Violence and Its Aftermath in Yaquina Narrative ↗

Publication: Fall 2008

Byram’s opening pages place Yaquina villages near the bay and along related waterways and identify the Yaquina as one of the ancestral peoples of today’s Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians. The article notes whose oral accounts it draws on.

Inspection: Supporting or limited review; see scope

Scope: The opening identification of the Yaquina, pre-mid-1850s settlement context, and introduction of the oral sources in Oregon Historical Quarterly 109(3).

Review recorded: November 20, 2026

Beach at Yaquina Bay, Newport, Oregon
Gary Halvorson, Oregon State Archives

Source & image record ↗ · CC BY 4.0

Gary Halvorson’s 2004 photograph shows the beach at Yaquina Bay in Newport. The bay provides geographic context for the Yaquina homeland described in the Oregon curriculum and Byram’s study. The Atlas resized the original for the directory card and photo viewer.
